docket.challenge_claim: Both challenges hold that the span splices Hebrew from 4:3 and quotes its translation line with no ketiv/qere disclosure anywhere in the row, so the two declared false positives should be refuted rather than confirmed; one adds that the plural jackal reading silently adopts one of the two competing readings.
docket.grounds: Byte-verified and convergent - one defect, two framings. 4:3 is one of the book's two doubled-note ketiv/qere verses (inventory: 22 notes over 20 verses, 2 notes at 4:3), and both pairs stand in the source line: unpointed ketiv תנין against pointed qere תַּנִּים֙, and unpointed ketiv כי ענים against pointed qere כַּיְעֵנִ֖ים (oshb:Lam.4.3; ketiv forms byte-exact as consonantal skeletons, qere forms at byte tier). device_notes splices בַּת עַמִּ֣י from that same verse at byte tier and boundary_rationale quotes its translation line, verbatim on my own check; no field of the row carries any ketiv/qere disclosure. The disclosure requirement carries no materiality exception, so both declared false positives are refuted and stand as confirmed defects. The added point holds as well: the rationale's nursing jackals is plural, which is the qere, against a singular ketiv - one of two competing readings presented as the text at the very verse where the row also anchors its recurrence claim. The remainder of the row checks: the opening cry is verse-initial at 4:1 (sweep: 4 verses book-wide, verse-initial in 3, the non-initial site being 4:2); the two-token daughter-of-my-people phrase stands in 5 verses book-wide (2:11, 3:48, 4:3, 4:6, 4:10), matching the cited digit; letters aleph through vav are positions 1-6 of this chapter's pe-before-ayin order and are correctly not called the standard one; every verse of the span carries a mark, each disclosed as single-witness, with the preceding PE at 3:66 named and never conflated with samekh; and all three quoted translation lines are verbatim.
docket.remedy: device_notes: add a ketiv/qere disclosure for 4:3 naming both notes as single-witness apparatus and stating which of the two readings the jackals wording follows, or restate the wording so that it chooses neither. boundary_rationale: keep the quoted translation line and carry the same disclosure in-field, so that the splice and the quote each sit beside it. Tests the cure must pass: with the splice and the translation quote retained, the prose-dual and quote-coverage disclosure warnings that raised the original two flags must return zero; and the two queue entries must be re-dispositioned from declared false positive to confirmed and repaired.

docket.challenge_claim: One challenge holds that the rejected alternative names content not found in the cited earlier verses; the converging challenge calls that same alternative unrealizable as a contiguous span, and adds that the front seam rests on topic alone with no person shift disclosed and that the divine-name note misplaces the 4:11 site.
docket.grounds: The two rejected-alternative findings are one defect in two framings, and it holds. The nobles term stands only at 4:7, נְזִירֶ֨יהָ֙ (oshb:Lam.4.7, byte tier; sweep: 1 verse book-wide), outside this span; 4:12-4:14 carry the disbelieving kings of the earth, the sins of prophets and priests, and blood-polluted wanderers, with no nobles and no elders falling; the only elders term in the wider group is the qere וּזְקֵנִ֖ים (oshb:Lam.4.16, byte tier), later than 4:15 rather than earlier. An alternative that ends the group at 4:14 while keeping 4:15 with the nobles therefore describes no contiguous span the witness carries, and its content cannot be checked against the witnessed verses. The divine-name note fails on bytes: the name stands at 4:11, 4:16 and 4:20 in this poem (sweep: 3 verses in the chapter, 32 book-wide), and 4:11 is the verse immediately before this span's onset, so under an exact tiling it closes the preceding unit and cannot have opened it; the same sentence also refers to a neighbouring unit positionally rather than by verse. The front-seam finding holds with one refinement. There is no voice or addressee change across 4:11 and 4:12 - no first-plural element stands anywhere in 4:1-4:16 (sweep: 0 verses; the two plural-ending tokens there, הֶאֱמִ֨ינוּ֙ (oshb:Lam.4.12, byte tier) and חָנָֽנוּ (oshb:Lam.4.16, byte tier), are third-plural perfects) - and neither corroborating layer can discriminate a seam inside this poem, since every verse opens a new acrostic letter and every verse carries a mark (sweep: 21 samekh and 1 pe over the poem's 22 verses). The refinement: the bytes do offer an undisclosed tier-1 ground the field could have argued, since 4:12 introduces new grammatical participants, מַלְכֵי אֶ֔רֶץ and יֹשְׁבֵ֣י תֵבֵ֑ל (oshb:Lam.4.12, byte tier), where the preceding verses run on the city and her people. The corrected finding is that the seam's tier-1 warrant is undisclosed and the confidence unhedged, not that no warrant exists. The ketiv/qere disclosure in the row is accurate: notes stand at 4:12 and 4:16 and nowhere else in the span, both unspliced.
docket.remedy: strongest_rejected_alternative: replace the unrealizable alternative with one naming a contiguous verse range the witness carries (for example a group closing at 4:13 weighed against one closing at 4:16), and either drop the nobles reference or anchor it to 4:7. device_notes: correct 'the mention at 4:11 that opened the group before it' to state that the site stands at 4:11, the verse immediately before this span, and re-anchor the sentence to verses rather than to a neighbouring unit. boundary_rationale: disclose the seam ground explicitly - either name the participant introduction at 4:12 as the tier-1 signal, or state that the seam is thematic, set frontier_flag_considered true and lower confidence accordingly. docket.challenge_claim: The seam taken is the byte-correct one but the case made for it is not: the tested alternative is called the more probable seam on a ground that refutes it, the first-plural onset claim ships without its digit, and the closing verse is retitled past its own bytes.
docket.grounds: All three findings verified. First, the onset claim is byte-true and undigited: no first-plural element stands anywhere in 4:1-4:16 (sweep: 0 verses; the two plural-ending tokens there are third-plural perfects), while 4:17-4:20 carry fifteen first-plural tokens over four consecutive verses (5, 5, 3 and 2 respectively). boundary_rationale asserts that the plural enters at the ayin line - an onset claim of the class that must carry an adjacent digit-bearing sweep naming object and unit - and carries none, which leaves the row's strongest evidence as its only uncounted claim. One refinement on the challenge's own count-object: the census mixes pronominal suffixes with first-plural verbal afformatives, צִפִּ֔ינוּ (oshb:Lam.4.17, byte tier) and אָמַ֔רְנוּ (oshb:Lam.4.20, byte tier), so the object is properly named as first-plural elements rather than suffixes; the digits and the zero result are unaffected. Second, the tested alternative is self-refuting and internally incoherent: the field names 4:16 as the more probable seam while the row takes 4:17, and grounds that preference on 4:16's verbs staying third person about them rather than us - which is the strongest argument for the seam actually taken. The only plural-looking form at 4:16 is חָנָֽנוּ (oshb:Lam.4.16, byte tier), a third-plural perfect. Third, the gloss exceeds its splice: the field calls 4:20 the king's capture, but the spliced phrase is מְשִׁ֣יחַ יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Lam.4.20, byte tier), the book's only anointed term (sweep: 1 verse book-wide), and the row's own translation quote renders it the anointed of Yahweh; the one king term in this poem, מַלְכֵי אֶ֔רֶץ (oshb:Lam.4.12, byte tier), denotes the nations' kings. The ketiv/qere handling is sound: the pair עודינה against qere עוֹדֵ֨ינוּ֙ at 4:17 is spliced with both forms and disclosed in-field, and the inventory carries no other note and no paseq inside the span; the letters at positions 17-20 and the mark disclosures from 4:16 through 4:20 are correct.
docket.remedy: boundary_rationale: attach a digit-bearing sweep to the plural-onset claim naming its object and unit (first-plural elements: 0 verses across 4:1-4:16; 15 tokens over the four verses 4:17-4:20), and replace 'the king's capture' with a gloss no wider than the splice. strongest_rejected_alternative: restate the alternative so that its stated ground would favour the alternative rather than the seam actually taken, and remove 'the more probable seam' unless the seam itself is moved. Tests the cure must pass: the exclusivity and onset arm must find an adjacent digit-bearing sweep naming object and unit; every rejected alternative must be argued on a ground that would favour it; and gloss extent must not exceed splice extent when the sentence is read back whole.

docket.challenge_claim: The span, its address evidence and its flagged concern all hold, but the cohesion ground given for keeping the two verses together names shared vocabulary that stands in one verse apiece, the genre label ascribes a speech class the book nowhere carries, and a substrate-signal key names the poem-closing mark.
docket.grounds: The cohesion finding stands: the cup term כּ֔וֹס (oshb:Lam.4.21, byte tier) stands in 4:21 only (sweep: 1 verse book-wide) and 4:21 carries no iniquity term at all, while עֲוֺנֵךְ֙ (oshb:Lam.4.22, byte tier) stands twice in 4:22 and nowhere in 4:21 - so the shared cup and iniquity vocabulary offered as the reason for one span does not exist. What is genuinely shared is the two-token address to Edom, בַּת אֱד֔וֹם (oshb:Lam.4.21, byte tier), standing in both verses (sweep: 2 verses book-wide, both inside this span), which the row's device note already names. The refinement is on the challenge's own census: its figure of 4 verses for the iniquity term matches neither reading of its object - the suffixed token stands in 2 verses (2:14, 4:22), and the lexeme, swept with a finals-normalized needle, stands in 5 (2:14, 4:6, 4:13, 4:22, 5:7); the four-verse figure drops עֲוֺ֣ן (oshb:Lam.4.6, byte tier) because a medial-nun needle does not match the final nun there. The genre finding stands: 4:21 runs on second-feminine-singular imperatives שִׂ֤ישִׂי וְשִׂמְחִי֙ (oshb:Lam.4.21, byte tier) and second-feminine-singular prefix forms, and 4:22 on third-masculine-singular verbs with second-feminine-singular suffixes; no first-person divine speech and no messenger formula stands anywhere in this book, so calling the unit an oracle ascribes a speech class the witness does not carry. The signal-key finding needs refining rather than upholding as framed: the listed key names the poem's closing PE mark but does not use the barred parashah prefix, so it is not a straight taxonomy violation; the substance holds, in that a tier-3 single-witness mark class travels into the structured signal list under a different prefix without the caveats its disclosure requires, while the row's prose already carries a compliant version - prefix evasion, low on its own. The declared false positives are confirmed genuine: the note at 4:21 attaches to the dwelling participle, ketiv יושבתי against qere יוֹשֶׁ֖בֶת (oshb:Lam.4.21), not to the spliced address, and device_notes discloses the note, so the writer's disposition stands. The span is not contested and the one-apostrophe-or-two question stays held open at low-side confidence with the frontier flag set.
docket.remedy: strongest_rejected_alternative: replace 'the shared cup/iniquity vocabulary across both verses' with the ground the bytes carry - the two-token address to Edom standing in both verses - with its digit-bearing sweep (2 verses book-wide, both inside this span). literature_type_guess: drop 'oracle' and keep the address class, an apostrophe to Edom in the poet's own voice, since the substrate carries no divine speech. observed_substrate_signals: remove the key naming the poem-closing mark and leave that disclosure to prose, where the single-witness and weak-corroboration caveats can travel with it. Tests the cure must pass: every cohesion ground must name a term a sweep places in both verses it is said to join, with its object and unit; every genre or speech-class label must be re-derived from the pointed forms; and no structured signal key may name a parashah mark class under any prefix.

docket.challenge_claim: Convergent on one row. One challenge holds that the close taken at 5:11 carries no disclosed voice, addressee or discourse-frame marker, and that the ground used to set aside a cut after 5:6 would equally indict the chosen close. The other holds that the close cuts a byte-marked four-verse block after its first member with no weighing from either side, that both petition-onset digits misname what they count, and that the onset is called a doubled imperative where the verse carries three.
docket.grounds: Same defect at the seam in both challenges; the digit and form-class items are distinct additions carried by only one of them. SEAM (upheld, tier-1). Re-derived from the pointed text of the whole poem: 5:11-5:14 each open with a bare plural human-group noun - נָשִׁים֙ (oshb:Lam.5.11, byte tier), שָׂרִים֙ (oshb:Lam.5.12, byte tier), בַּחוּרִים֙ (oshb:Lam.5.13, byte tier), זְקֵנִים֙ (oshb:Lam.5.14, byte tier) - each followed by a third-plural verb, and none of the four carries a first-person-plural form (sweep: 0 first-plural-suffix or first-plural-verb tokens over those 4 verses; the single plural-ending token at 5:11 is a third-plural perfect). That is a tier-1 participant-run repetition straddling the unit's own close, disclosed nowhere. CORRECTION to the challenge's exclusivity: neither test is exclusive alone - the same verse-initial bare plural human-group noun stands at 5:3 and 5:8 (sweep: 6 verses in this poem carry that onset: 5:3, 5:8, 5:11, 5:12, 5:13, 5:14), and 5:18 also carries no first-plural form (sweep: 5 verses of 5:1-5:18 carry none: 5:11, 5:12, 5:13, 5:14, 5:18); it is the CONJUNCTION of the two tests that is exclusive, holding in exactly 4 verses, 5:11-5:14, the only consecutive run of any length in the poem (sweep: 4 verses of 22). The unit's own cited texture does not close at 5:11 either: the divine name stands at 5:1, 5:19 and 5:21 and nowhere between (sweep: 3 verses in this poem), so the absence of further direct address runs unbroken through 5:18 and cannot mark a close at 5:11. current_row.boundary_rationale: The catalog continues from economic loss into social and personal violation: princes hanged, young men set to milling and stumbling under loads, elders gone from the gate. The group turns from external causes to the community's own confession at its center, נָֽפְלָה֙ עֲטֶ֣רֶת — the crown fallen (oshb:Lam.5.16, byte tier) — “The crown has fallen from our head.” (web:Lam.5.16). It closes on the desolation named directly, הַר צִיּוֹן֙ (oshb:Lam.5.18, byte tier), “the mountain of Zion, which is desolate” (web:Lam.5.18), the verse carrying this poem's own parashah mark, disclosed as tier-3 weak and single-witness.

docket.challenge_claim: The span is byte-clean on every seam, quotation, census and disclosure test except its closing note, which calls 5:21 the unit's centre and says the two divine-name sites frame the petition between them: the span runs four verses so 5:21 is its third, the verse between the two sites is a why-question, and the span's only petition imperative stands at 5:21 itself.
docket.grounds: Upheld in substance, refined on the challenge's own exclusivity digit. ARITHMETIC (upheld, tier-1 address signal with a false positional gloss): the span runs 4 verses and 5:21 is its third, so the centre placement is false to the span's own count; the divine name stands at 5:19 and 5:21 and at neither 5:20 nor 5:22 (sweep: 3 verses in this poem - 5:1, 5:19, 5:21), and what stands between the two sites is the why-question of 5:20, whose verbs are second-masculine-singular imperfects carrying first-plural object suffixes - not a petition. So the framed material is not the petition, and the petition stands at one of the frames. REFINEMENT: the challenge calls the return-imperative the span's only petition imperative; the bytes carry a second one in the same verse, חַדֵּ֥שׁ (oshb:Lam.5.21, byte tier; a ketiv/qere verse, the variant standing at the return-verb, which the unit splices and discloses). Both imperatives sit at 5:21, so the finding survives intact and only its exclusivity digit is wrong - an object-of-the-digit correction, not a rescue of the unit. The rest of what the challenge confirms reproduces here: the address return at 5:19 opens the span after verses carrying no divine name; the one paseq site across the fourth and fifth poems stands at 5:21 (sweep: 1 seg, count-only, single-witness); the ketiv/qere note at 5:21 is disclosed in the field carrying the splice; and this poem carries no acrostic, none being claimed.
docket.remedy: device_notes: replace the centre wording with the span's own arithmetic (5:21 is the third of the span's four verses) and re-state the frame - the two address sites stand at 5:19 and 5:21 with the why-question of 5:20 between them, and the span's petition imperatives (return and renew) both stand at 5:21, at one of the frames rather than between them. TEST the cure must pass - the test that killed the original: every positional word reproduces against the span's own verse count, and any material described as framed is the material actually standing between the two cited sites.

current_row.boundary_rationale: The poem turns from catalog to hymn: אַתָּ֤ה יְהוָה֙ (oshb:Lam.5.19, byte tier) reopens direct address to YHWH after the descriptive verses behind it, “You, Yahweh, remain forever.” (web:Lam.5.19). The petition “Turn us to yourself, Yahweh, and we will be turned.” (web:Lam.5.21) carries its own ketiv-qere pair, ונשוב וְֽנָשׁ֔וּבָה (oshb:Lam.5.21, byte tier; the inventory's own K/Q note here), both readings meaning turn or return. Whether 5:19-5:22 forms a close of its own or reads on from the petition before it is held open rather than decided; the poem's closing word stays unresolved, “you have utterly rejected us” (web:Lam.5.22).
